pr_title: Introduce Elasticsearch PostingFormat based on Lucene 90 positing format using PFOR
pr_body:
Lucene 9.9 has introduced a new posting format that uses FOR instead of PFOR. Elasticsearch prefers the  former format, therefore we introduce it as a our own posting format here.

fixes https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/103002
pr_comments: Hi @iverase, I've created a changelog YAML for you.

A question about the 1st comment "Lucene 9.9 has introduced a new posting format that uses FOR instead of PFOR. Elasticsearch prefers the former format, therefore we introduce it as a our own posting format here." I think ES prefers the _later_ format?

issue_context.title: Disk usage has increased in the nightly Logging benchmark
issue_context.body:
Disk usage has increased in the nightly Logging benchmark [1] (on 2023-12-04), from 182GB to 190GB. A little more than 4%. This lines up with the bump to Lucene 9.9.0 in Elasticsearch. 

![Screenshot 2023-12-05 at 17 36 34](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/assets/62058229/84d6d174-07aa-46f1-b83d-f4ce3b63ae95)

Lucene 9.9.0 has changed postings back to using FOR (from PFOR)[2] . This is the likely change that has resulted in the additional usage.

[1] https://elasticsearch-benchmarks.elastic.co/#tracks/logging/nightly/default/30d - look at `nightly-elastic/logs-io`
[2] https://github.com/apache/lucene/pull/12741

Note from the Lucene 9.9.0 changelog: "GITHUB#12696: Change Postings back to using FOR in Lucene99PostingsFormat. Freqs, positions and offset keep using PFOR."
comments: Elasticsearch can add back PFOR encoding for posting, in our own codec.
Maybe a heuristic for using PFOR would be if an index is backing index of a data stream? (`mapperService.mappingLookup().isDataStreamTimestampFieldEnabled()` would do the trick)

review_comments: Add a quick note that it was introduced to preserve PFOR space efficiency when Lucene switched back to FOR in 9.9?
